E°cell = E°(reduction) − E°(oxidation) = 1.51 − (−0.49) = +2.00 V.

(ii) E° is positive, so the reaction is spontaneous as written.

(i) The diagram needs a DC power supply, connecting wires, two electrodes in a container of electrolyte (FeBr2(l) or FeBr2(aq)), the anode (+) and cathode (−) labelled, and the electrolyte labelled.

(ii) In the electrolyte, ions carry the current: cations move to the cathode (−) and anions to the anode (+). In the wires, electrons flow from the negative to the positive terminal of the supply through the external circuit.

(iii) Cathode: H2, because H+/H2O is reduced more easily than Fe2+ (Fe is more reactive; E° of H2 is less negative). Anode: O2, because in dilute solution Br− is at low concentration, so water/OH− is oxidized in preference.

(iv) Br2 at the anode (Fe at the cathode also accepted).

(v) A high [Br−] shifts Br2 + 2e− ⇌ 2Br− to the left, so 2Br− → Br2 + 2e− is favoured and Br− is discharged instead of water.

(ii) CaCO3(s) + H2SO4(aq) → CaSO4(s) + H2O(l) + CO2(g). CaSO4(aq) is also accepted. The second mark is for correct state symbols.
